title: Downstream certified rungs (dipole, HF-overlap) consume gap_bracket at a single uncorroborated M — measured 500x escape upstream
description:
specs/BACKLOG.md line ~135, "Certified-bounds arc" section (scout probe). Claim: certified_gaps'
"zero escapes at M>=6" finding is a property of its three original test systems, not a general
property of M>=6 — on stretched/asymmetric H4 the self-mode lower certificate escapes and stays
escaped through M=12. gap_selfcheck.py already catches every escape it's been wired into. But three
downstream call sites call gap_bracket at a single M with NO corroboration from gap_selfcheck:
certified_dipole.py:88, hf_overlap_certificate.py:58, hf_overlap_subspace.py:117 (not re-verified
this session — re-grep before editing).

Scout-probe evidence already in the backlog: linear H4 at R=3.0 A, M=6 -> Delta_lo in [0.590, 0.599]
vs true gap 0.0012 Ha, a ~500x escape.

Check (killable): sweep those three geometries/call sites through certified_dipole and
certify_hf_overlap at M in {6,8,12,16}, reference = exact reachable dipole/overlap. Dies (informative
either way) if no downstream escape is found — worth recording as "the bounds are robust to their own
gap input being wrong," which is itself a real finding.

Reuse: gap_selfcheck.self_checked_gap_from is the fix if the escape propagates downstream.

Caveat / do in the same pass but don't conflate with the headline: two latent crashes were found en
route by the original scout — a spectral_width ArpackError on square H4 where mu_z == 0 identically,
and a zero-half-width epsilon floor on HeH+. Fix them alongside this if hit, but report them
separately, not dressed up as the main finding.

Cost: cheap (~2 min, all systems are 8-qubit).
acceptance_criteria: certified_dipole, hf_overlap_certificate, hf_overlap_subspace swept at M in {6,8,12,16} on the stretched/asymmetric H4 geometries where the upstream escape was found; either a downstream escape is demonstrated and gap_selfcheck.self_checked_gap_from is wired in as the fix, or the absence of an escape is recorded as a positive robustness finding. The two latent crashes (ArpackError, epsilon floor) are reported.
close_reason: Downstream sweep (48 checks, 4 geometries x M in {6,8,12,16} x 3 call sites) found zero escapes -- positive robustness finding, gap_selfcheck not wired in. Fixed latent ArpackError crash on zero-operator spectral_width (regression test added). HeH+ epsilon-floor crash investigated (40 checks) but not reproduced as an exception. Full evidence: sandbox-handoffs/chem-52i.md

title: operator_one_norms (certified_dipole_noise.py) has the same identity-inflation bug SPEC_lambda_meas_identity already fixed elsewhere
description:
specs/BACKLOG.md line ~119 (verified in code). Confirmed 2026-09-28:
certified_dipole_noise.py's operator_one_norms does `lam = float(np.abs(op.coeffs).sum())`, i.e. sums
|coeff| over ALL Pauli terms including the identity, on both lambda_A and lambda_{A^2}. Its own
docstring says it "mirrors certified_noise.hamiltonian_one_norms (same construction)" — that function
was the one SPEC_lambda_meas_identity already corrected to exclude the identity term, because the
identity contributes zero variance (it's a constant shift, not a fluctuating observable) and so
inflates the Pauli 1-norm without inflating the actual noise. operator_one_norms was apparently missed
when that fix landed elsewhere.

Claim: the same zero-variance argument applies here, so operator_one_norms inflates lambda_A the same
way, and the certified-dipole noise numbers in specs/SPEC_certified_dipole_noise.md inherit the
inflation.

Check (killable): exclude the identity term from operator_one_norms and re-run
SPEC_certified_dipole_noise's coverage sweep (tests/test_certified_dipole_noise_spec.py or equivalent).
Dies if lambda_A is unchanged — a traceless dipole operator in this frame would have no identity term,
which would make the mirror harmless and this a non-issue.

Caveat: SPEC_certified_dipole_noise records a fragile vacuous/non-vacuous boundary and a "double-
spending the Delta_lo margin" finding. Narrowing lambda_A moves those numbers, so this needs its own
before/after analysis of whether a recorded finding flips — do not fix it blind without re-checking
that spec's headline.

Cost: cheap.
acceptance_criteria: operator_one_norms excludes the identity term (or is proven not to carry one for the dipole operator, in which case that's recorded and the code is left alone); SPEC_certified_dipole_noise's coverage sweep is re-run and any moved finding (including the vacuous-boundary / margin-double-spend numbers) is documented, not silently overwritten.
close_reason: Fix was already landed by a prior worker session (committed in 5c5c6db); this session independently verified it (reran the 4 G1-G4 gates, reran the before/after scratch script, cross-checked all SPEC §5/§10 numbers) and fixed two citation-only inaccuracies in the SPEC's own revision note. No code/numeric changes needed beyond what was already there.

title: H-chain thermodynamic limit to n~40 with a systematic-inclusive error bar
description:
The committed headline e_inf = -0.539967 ± 0.000107 Ha/atom (n<=16) misses the published Simons/Motta DMRG STO-6G TDL value -0.540493 (PRX 7, 031059) by ~5x its own error bar (specs/BACKLOG.md:440-452). The ± is a fit stderr that tracks scatter, not the finite-size bias: e_inf drifts monotonically with n_max. The uncommitted 2026-07-04 run to n<=20 gives -0.540080 ± 0.000075, but its largest points are out of regime (stderr 0.83 mHa at n=20, 2.4 mHa at n=22; E/atom is non-monotone at n=22), and its bulk per-site estimate (-0.540818) disagrees with the 1/n fit by 0.74 mHa/atom. Note that SPEC_hchain_largen2.md:3-9 still says 'not yet executed'. That is stale: it was run, it cost ~21 h to n=20 on canonical orbitals, and it was killed at n=24.

WORK (after the localized-orbital bead shows the cost drop): uv run python benchmark_hchain_tdl.py --protocol ramp --localize --ns 8,10,12,16,20,24,28,32,40 --bond-dims 250,500,1000 --threads 4 --stack-mem-gb 6. The driver is resumable. Run the largest n last and stop cleanly if the time budget runs out; a clean n<=32 result beats a killed n<=40 one. Report e_inf from BOTH routes, the 1/n fit and bulk_per_site_energy, across several fit windows.

(3) The 1/n fit and bulk_per_site_energy agree to <0.1 mHa/atom. (4) e_inf is quoted with a systematic-inclusive bar (the spread across fit windows, not the fit stderr) and compared with -0.540493, stated as 'within' or 'outside' that bar with no hedging. (5) The per-n table is vendored into a tracked file and read by a spec gate; SPEC_hchain_largen2.md status is corrected, and BACKLOG.md:440 is resolved or updated. (6) If the result still disagrees with Motta, record that; don't tune the fit window to close the gap.

Headline e_inf = -0.540353 ± 0.000192 Ha/atom (8-fit envelope + max stderr). Motta -0.540493 is INSIDE (0.73 bar). All four a+b/n+c/n^2 fits give -0.540492..-0.540496. LOO 0.037 mHa PASS; bulk vs a+b/n fit 0.232 mHa FAIL (reported: the 1/n form is wrong at n<=40). n=48/56 were OOM-killed at 15 GiB. The old headline -0.539967 ± 0.000107 is superseded. title: H-chain DMRG: localized site orbitals, validated against FCI, with a cost probe at n=20
description:
Every H-chain DMRG run so far used canonical, delocalized RHF orbitals: benchmark_hchain_tdl.py integrals() passes mf.mo_coeff straight through, and dmrg_reference.py calls initialize_system(orb_sym=None) with no localization or reordering. For a 1D chain, delocalized orbitals make entanglement grow with n. That plausibly explains why the large-n run cost ~21 h for n<=20 on the laptop (logs/hchain_pipeline.log: n=8..20 took 2026-07-04 04:50 to 07-05 01:53; the n=22/24 stage was killed after ~19.5 h), and why SPEC_hchain_largen recorded 'D needed grows with n'. The literature H-chain benchmarks (Hachmann/Chan; Motta et al. PRX 7, 031059) use localized orbitals. This is an INFERENCE from the code, not yet measured; this bead measures it.

WORK: add a --localize option to integrals() (Löwdin/meta-Löwdin orthogonalized site orbitals over the FULL basis, in chain order). A unitary rotation of the full space leaves the FCI energy unchanged exactly, and DMRG energies converge to the same limit. Then run the cost probe: n=20, D=400, canonical vs localized, same sweeps, recording the discarded weight, the energy and the wall time for each.

CLOUD SETUP: `uv sync --extra dmrg --extra test` (Linux x86_64; do NOT install the gpu extra; there is no CUDA). block2 segfaults when it shares a process with pyscf/qiskit-aer, so run each spec gate in its own process (`make gates`, or `scripts/run_gates.sh`; `GATE_JOBS=1` if one gets SIGKILLed). data/ is gitignored, so a fresh clone has none of the recorded CSVs: regenerate what you need, and put every number you report into a TRACKED file (the spec, or a vendored table the gate reads), never only into data/. Deliver the result as a branch + PR, not a push to main.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Localized-orbital FCI matches canonical FCI at n=8,10,12 to <1e-8 Ha, added as a spec gate next to G1 in tests/test_hchain_tdl_spec.py. (2) At n=10 and 12, localized DMRG matches FCI to <1e-6 Ha. (3) Recorded for the n=20, D=400 probe, both bases: E, discarded weight, wall time and threads. (4) A one-line verdict in SPEC_hchain_largen2.md: does localization cut the D needed at fixed accuracy, and by how much? If it does NOT, say so plainly; the downstream beads then need re-scoping, not a bigger machine.
close_reason: Done via PR #39 (merged into certkit-integration at 801b445). Löwdin site orbitals behind --localize; FCI invariant to <1e-10 at n=8,10,12; localized G1 converged regime; D=1000 n=12 within 2.2e-11 of FCI. n=20 probe (Xeon, 4 threads): canonical D=400 is 6.4e-3 Ha above the best energy after 572 s without converging; localized D=100 reaches 5.7e-8 in 38 s. D cut >=8x, time >=29x (both lower bounds). Independently reproduced 2026-09-24 in a Linux arm64 container: the 3 G1 gates pass and localized n=20 D=100 gives E=-10.825878811 (identical). Also fixed a latent bug: fci_energy silently returned unconverged Davidson energies (follow-up chem-3f8). macOS DMRG is currently broken by a duplicate libomp (chem-dfe), unrelated to this change.

title: compile_from_gcs labels geometries by nearest-CASCI match, destroying the reference check
description: compile_from_gcs.py recovers which geometry produced each GCS result by computing local CASCI energies for every candidate coordinate and taking the argmin of |E_solver - E_CASCI| (accepting under 1e-4 Ha), with a comment asserting the closest match is 'mathematically guaranteed to be correct'. It is not: it is circular. The coordinate label is derived FROM the reference, so any later comparison of that dataset against CASCI is guaranteed to agree to <1e-4 by construction and can no longer falsify anything. identify_family_by_energy() compounds this with hardcoded energy windows. This violates the repo's falsifiable-honesty rule that every result carries a reference that could kill it. Fix: have the worker persist the request geometry into the result blob (or key blobs by a content hash of the request) so provenance is recorded, not inferred.
acceptance_criteria: result JSON carries the originating molecule/basis/active_space; compile path reads provenance rather than matching energies; any CASCI comparison is then an independent check
close_reason: Provenance now stated by the producer: EnergyRequest takes optional bounded metadata, worker stamps molecule/basis/active_space/mode/krylov_dim/job_id/metadata into every result blob, compile_from_gcs reads those labels and skips (never guesses) provenance-less blobs. Circular identify_family_by_energy + CASCI-argmin matching deleted along with the duplicated geometry tables. --verify makes the CASCI comparison a real independent check on bracket containment. 14 tests in tests/test_certchem_provenance.py. Commit 51d92d9.

title: run_grand_sweep: ethylene torsion submits 7 identical geometries
description: generate_experiments()['ethylene_torsion'] computes rad = deg*pi/180 and never uses it; y_r/z_r are hardcoded constants (y*0.86, z*0.50), so all 7 torsion angles 0-90deg produce a byte-identical molecule string. Verified: 7 points -> 1 distinct geometry. The 'diradical transition state at 90 degrees' this family claims to probe is never computed. compile_from_gcs.py:ethylene_geom(deg) has the same defect and ignores its deg argument, so the recovery path would happily label 7 copies of one energy as a torsion curve. Fix: rotate the second CH2 plane by rad about the C-C axis.
acceptance_criteria: 7 torsion points yield 7 distinct geometries; energy at 90deg differs measurably from 0deg; a test asserts len(set(geoms))==7
close_reason: ethylene_geometry(deg) now rotates the C2 methylene about the C-C axis; 7 angles -> 7 distinct geometries, dihedral matches request, bond lengths/angles invariant. CASCI(2,2)/sto-3g barrier +86.0 kcal/mol, monotonic. compile_from_gcs imports the single generator. Gate in tests/test_ethylene_torsion.py, verified failing pre-fix. Commit 574b8e8.

title: Symmetry-adapted T2 to evaluate the chem-3z8 PQG+T2 kill test at n=10-12
description: chem-3z8 (SPEC_hchain_vsdp_bracket) certified PQG brackets for H_n n=2-16: killed, 2.49 mHa/atom at n=12 and growing. title: Is NbN's flagged 'hard multireference' low-spin (7,7) sector actually hard, or was it just never run?
description:
specs/BACKLOG.md line ~529, "Scale, references, harnesses" section. Claim: SPEC_nbn_dmrg_reference
sections 2 and 7 flag the low-spin nelec=(7,7) sector (comb(14,7)^2 ~= 1.18e7 determinants, reportedly
3.5 mHa above the ground state) as needing genuinely large bond dimension to resolve -- but per the
backlog, this sector has never actually been RUN or gated, only flagged as presumed-hard.

Check (killable/confirmable): run the identical A'/B' DMRG schedule pair already used elsewhere in this
spec (reuse load_nbn_cas and all four existing SCHEDULES -- no new machinery needed), but force
nelec=(7,7) explicitly. The "actually easy" kill: if discarded weight dw(D=300) < 1e-7 AND the spread
across schedules is < 1e-5 Ha, the sector converges trivially and the "hard multireference benchmark"
framing is wrong -- it just needed to be run. The "genuinely hard" confirm: if dw > 1e-5 at D=300 OR
|E_A' - E_B'| > 0.1 mHa (schedule-dependent, a classic strong-correlation signature), the framing holds
-- and then the follow-up question is whether the named 3.5 mHa sector gap survives at fully converged
D, or whether it inverts/changes as D increases (a stalled-schedule mislabel, per this repo's own
history with chem-4e9/chem-mjz, is a real risk to rule out here specifically).

Cost: cheap as a diagnostic (~2 min per schedule at D<=300, block2's own process per the repo's
mandatory DMRG process-isolation rule -- do NOT run this in the same pytest process as anything that
imports pyscf or qiskit-aer). Only expensive if the sector proves genuinely hard and needs D>300 to
converge, in which case treat it as a separate, larger follow-on rather than scope-creeping this bead.

Caveat (author's own expectation): half-expected to be killed (sector turns out easy). Either outcome
is the deliverable -- do not treat "it was easy" as a null result, it directly corrects a claim
currently standing in SPEC_nbn_dmrg_reference.
acceptance_criteria: All four existing SCHEDULES run against nelec=(7,7) forced, each in its own process per the block2 isolation rule, capped at D<=300 and --stack-mem-gb<=6 per this repo's compute envelope. dw(D=300) and cross-schedule spread |E_A'-E_B'| reported. The easy-vs-hard verdict is recorded, and if hard, whether the 3.5 mHa sector gap survives at the largest converged D actually reached (with any stalled-vs-converged ambiguity explicitly checked, given this repo's prior chem-4e9/chem-mjz history).
notes: Already answered before this bead was filed, by chem-dc7/chem-g1i/chem-czw (SPEC_nbn_low_spin.md Table 2/G4): (7,7) sector is soft (dw->3e-10 by D=1200), not hard. Re-verified fresh this session on new hardware: uv run pytest -q tests/test_nbn_low_spin_spec.py (2 passed, 492.55s) and tests/test_nbn_dmrg_reference_spec.py (4 passed, 355.03s). Fixed stale 'never run'/'out of scope' text in SPEC_nbn_dmrg_reference.md sections 2/7/8 and moved the duplicate BACKLOG.md open item to Done with explanation. Full writeup in sandbox-handoffs/chem-csf.md.

This session independently re-verified that finding fresh on new hardware (tests/test_nbn_low_spin_spec.py, tests/test_nbn_dmrg_reference_spec.py both green) and fixed the stale SPEC_nbn_dmrg_reference.md text and BACKLOG.md entry that caused the duplicate filing. title: The 62x THC lambda penalty (SPEC_thc_lambda) may be a collocation-point artifact -- lambda_ladder.fit_thc's existing nonlinear fit has never been scored with the native thc_lambda
description:
specs/BACKLOG.md line ~391, "Fault-tolerant stack" section. Claim: SPEC_thc_lambda locks
lambda_THC ~= 62x lambda_DF as a deliberate, already-published finding, and puts optimized
(non-random) collocation point selection explicitly out of scope as "research-grade." But
lambda_ladder.fit_thc (confirm this function still exists at this name before starting) is a nonlinear
Levenberg-Marquardt THC fit that PREDATES that spec -- it has only ever been scored against a
brute-force Pauli-string lambda (which caps usable system size at roughly 4 orbitals and conflates two
different 1-norm conventions), never against the spec's own NATIVE thc_lambda function.

Check (killable): at matched THC rank and matched reconstruction error (<1e-6), compare random
collocation vs structured collocation vs fit_thc's nonlinear collocation, all scored with the native
thc_lambda, against df_lambda as the baseline. Dies (the ">=5x below random" half) if nonlinear
collocation does not land at least 5x below random collocation -- meaning the 62x penalty runs deeper
than "nobody optimized the collocation points." Opposite-direction kill: if nonlinear collocation
actually BEATS df_lambda outright, SPEC_thc_lambda's G4 gate must be revised, which that spec
explicitly says it invites.

Caveat (author's own stated expectation, and a real methodological risk): the >=5x half is
half-expected to be killed, because fit_thc minimizes RECONSTRUCTION ERROR, not lambda directly -- it
is lambda-blind by construction and may land anywhere in lambda-space regardless of how good the
reconstruction is. That would arguably be the sharper finding either way: an error-optimal THC fit is
not automatically a lambda-optimal one, which lines up with the literature's ISDF approach choosing
collocation points for physical locality specifically, not reconstruction accuracy. fit_thc is
stochastic (random initialization) -- pin the random seed explicitly and never claim global optimality
from a single run.

Cost: medium (~600 Levenberg-Marquardt parameters at norb=7; cap the CI-gated version at norb<=6 to
keep it fast).
acceptance_criteria: thc_lambda computed for random, structured, and fit_thc collocation at matched rank and <1e-6 reconstruction error, norb<=6 for the CI gate; the >=5x-below-random and beats-df_lambda kill criteria both evaluated explicitly; if fit_thc is found to be lambda-blind (does not beat random by 5x), that is recorded as the finding rather than treated as a failed experiment; random seed pinned and reported.
close_reason: Gates G1-G4 pass (tests/test_thc_collocation_spec.py, 4 passed in 66.5s); independently re-ran the full corroboration sweep this session and recorded results in SPEC_thc_collocation.md §9 and sandbox-handoffs/chem-5oj.md. Kill A does not fire (fit_thc ~65-69x below random); Kill B fires at 4/5 seeds but every such run fails the <1e-6 reconstruction precondition by 4-5 orders of magnitude, so SPEC_thc_lambda G4 is not revised.

title: The identity term inflates the fault-tolerant (qubitization) 1-norm the same way it inflated the near-term one, twice already fixed there
description:
specs/BACKLOG.md line ~376, "Fault-tolerant stack" section (scout probe). Claim: SPEC_shift_both_sides
and SPEC_lambda_meas_identity already caught the identity Pauli term inflating the NEAR-TERM 1-norm
(twice, independently, in this repo's own history) but the FT/qubitization side has not been touched:
build_walk_operator loads every term from pauli_decompose into PREPARE, identity included, so the
1-norm lambda_1norm carries dead constant mass that costs T-gates for nothing.

Scout-probe evidence already in the backlog (fraction of lambda that is dead identity mass):
|c_I|/lambda = 30.1% (H2), 44.2% (LiH), 49.3% (N2 CAS(3,4)), 45.6% (H2O CAS(3,4)) -- these are large
fractions, not a rounding-level effect.

Fix concept: a constant term is free to subtract before qubitization and add back classically after --
combined with the FT-side finding, the honest driver 1-norm becomes lambda_eff = sqrt(lambda^2 - E_0^2)
with an optimal shift c*.

Check (the real falsifier, not just re-measuring the identity fraction): re-center the Hamiltonian
(subtract the optimal constant shift) and feed it through run_qpe end to end; confirm the REALIZED
error at fixed circuit depth t drops by the predicted factor. Dies if it does not drop as predicted.

Caveat (important, read before generalizing): the scout also found df_lambda (double-factorized) LOSING
to identity-EXCLUDED naive lambda on all four systems tested, which superficially looks like it flips
SPEC_scdf_lambda's G1(b) finding. It probably does NOT actually flip it -- DF's rotated-number-operator
LCU construction absorbs constant mass implicitly through a different mechanism, so the two lambda
values may simply not be directly comparable. "G1(b) is a vacuous/apples-to-oranges check" is the more
likely and still-valuable finding here -- do not report a flip without first checking whether the
comparison is even well-posed.

Cost: cheap.
acceptance_criteria: Identity-mass fraction re-confirmed on the four systems; Hamiltonian re-centered by the optimal constant shift; run_qpe re-run end to end at fixed t and the realized-error drop compared against the predicted lambda_eff = sqrt(lambda^2 - E_0^2) factor; the df_lambda / SPEC_scdf_lambda G1(b) comparability question is explicitly addressed (comparable-and-flipped, or not-comparable-and-vacuous) rather than left ambiguous.
close_reason: G1-G5 all green in tests/test_ft_identity_shift_spec.py; see sandbox-handoffs/chem-177.md for full evidence per acceptance criterion

title: Classical shadows estimate <H> and <H^2> from one dataset cheaper than the repo's lambda^2 noise model -- but do they buy Temple-bracket coverage?
description:
specs/BACKLOG.md line ~292, "Method rungs" section (scout probe). Claim: SPEC_certified_noise found
lambda_{H^2} >> lambda_H (H4: 63 vs 10), which makes the Temple lower bound the noise-expensive side of
the certified arc, and precision_cost's temple_bounds states outright that the <H^2> hardware cost is
unmodeled. Random-Pauli classical shadows estimate BOTH moments from the SAME measurement snapshots,
with HKP-style variance bounds reportedly below the repo's assumed lambda^2 model.

Scout-probe evidence already in the backlog, H4: shadow_norm/lambda^2 is a stable 0.35-0.42 across both
the H and H^2 operators. But the shadow_norm RATIO H^2/H is 29.3, vs the lambda-based ratio of 35.6 --
i.e. shadows do NOT remove the H^2-vs-H cost asymmetry, just shrink it somewhat.

Check (killable): G1, unbiasedness on the Krylov Ritz state (not just the HF state) within 4x stderr
at 16k snapshots. G2, dies if shadow_norm(H^2) >= lambda_{H^2}^2 (no efficiency win at all). G4, the
real test: feed shadow-estimated moments into the Temple bracket over 200 seeds -- kills the
"free lunch" reading if coverage is ALSO around 0.40 (i.e. the variational knife-edge problem is
estimator-independent, shadows just relabel it).

Caveat: comparing shadow_norm to lambda^2 compares two different upper bounds derived from two
different protocols -- that comparison alone is not sufficient. The gate must ALSO measure the
empirical single-shot variance directly, or the comparison is apples-to-oranges and the "cheaper" claim
is unsupported.

Reuse (cheap-to-medium cost): H^2 for H4 already has 1775 Pauli terms vs H's 185 (O(N^8) growth) --
record that seam honestly rather than hiding the term-count blowup.

Cost: cheap-to-medium.
acceptance_criteria: G1 unbiasedness confirmed on the Krylov Ritz state within 4x stderr at 16k snapshots. G2 shadow_norm(H^2) vs lambda_{H^2}^2 compared directly. G4: 200-seed Temple bracket coverage using shadow-estimated moments, compared to the lambda^2-model coverage (~0.40 baseline). Empirical single-shot variance measured directly, not inferred only from the norm comparison.
close_reason: G1-G4 gates pass (5/5, tests/test_shadow_temple_spec.py). G2 units bug fixed. G3 revised to honestly record an unpredicted finding: HKP shadow_norm bound holds for H but is reproducibly violated for H^2 (1.16-1.49x over 10 seeds), while the efficiency claim (beats lambda^2) survives for both. G4: shadow coverage (0.395) matches lambda^2-model coverage (0.385) -- no free lunch, Temple break is estimator-independent. Handoff: sandbox-handoffs/chem-loe.md. Committed cb1af45 on sandbox/chem-loe, not pushed.

title: ODMD repairs the Temple bracket's oracle-free premise at shallow M then silently breaks it at deeper M -- map where, not just whether
description:
specs/BACKLOG.md line ~278, "Method rungs" section (scout probe). Claim: SPEC_temple_bracket's
oracle-free error estimate epsilon = theta_1 - sigma_1 fails (violates its own premise) at M<=4, and
certified_gaps inherits that boundary as a known limitation. ODMD's E_1 estimate comes from the first
row of S, the Krylov overlap matrix the solver already measures -- no extra measurement needed -- and
substituting it repairs the premise at shallow M. BUT ODMD is explicitly non-variational, so there is
no depth guarantee that epsilon <= E_1 holds as M grows deeper.

Scout-probe evidence already in the backlog, H4: self-mode M=4 gives epsilon = -1.59181 Ha vs true
E_1 = -1.649658 Ha -- premise violated. ODMD at K=16 gives -1.653511 Ha, premise restored, bracket
width 1.02 mHa. But ODMD at K=20 gives -1.649481 Ha, which is 0.176 mHa ABOVE the true E_1 -- premise
violated again. So a DEEPER signal makes the certificate WORSE, not better -- the repair is not
monotone in depth.

Check (killable): G-a, confirm the repair is non-vacuous by checking self-mode actually IS violated at
M=4 on all three of the spec's reference systems (not just H4). G-b, the actual test: find a K at
which ODMD overshoots E_1, and confirm the bracket is recorded as INVALID at that K rather than
silently smoothed over or averaged away.

Caveat: the headline claim ("ODMD repairs the premise") is already known to be false-by-construction
once K is pushed far enough -- the K=20 overshoot proves it empirically for at least one system. The
deliverable here is a MEASURED MAP of where the substitution helps and where it silently breaks (as a
function of K, per system), not a clean certificate. Pairs with SPEC_odmd_uq's recorded blind spot:
single-signal resampling cannot see model bias, so it cannot itself flag the overshoot -- don't rely on
SPEC_odmd_uq's machinery to catch this failure mode.

Cost: medium.
acceptance_criteria: G-a: self-mode violation at M=4 confirmed (or not) on all three reference systems. G-b: the K-sweep locating ODMD's overshoot point is run per system and the bracket-invalid flag is verified to trigger there rather than being silently absorbed. A K-vs-validity map is produced and recorded (not just a pass/fail on one system).

title: Bound the higher roots of PDS's P_K(E) as excited-state estimates (moment_expansion.py currently discards all but the ground root)
description:
specs/BACKLOG.md line ~265, "Method rungs" section (verified in code + scout probe). Confirmed
2026-09-28: moment_expansion.py's pds_energy computes real_roots via np.roots(poly), then does
`return float(real_roots.min()) + offset` -- every root except the smallest is discarded.
SPEC_moment_pds section 7 names "higher roots as excited states" as a named follow-up that was never
implemented.

Claim: the j-th smallest real root of P_K(E) is a variational UPPER bound on the j-th reachable
eigenvalue, but converges roughly 1000x slower in K than the ground root does at fixed K.

Scout-probe evidence already in the backlog, H4: ground root goes 2.04 -> 0.002 mHa error over K=3..7,
while root_1 (first excited) only crawls from 553 -> 20.5 mHa error over the same K range.

Check (killable): the bound claim dies if any root_j < E_j - 1e-9 Ha (would violate the variational
property, a hard error). The usefulness claim dies if PDS(K=8)'s first excited root is not within
1.6 mHa of the true E_1 on H4.

Reuse: a ~3-line pds_roots sibling function returning the full sorted real-root array (not just min())
is the only new code needed. Degeneracy handling should follow SPEC_qksd_excited R1's convention:
match roots to reference eigenvalues as a SORTED SET, never by positional index.

Caveat (author's own prediction, worth taking seriously): index-matching is expected to be killed on
near-degenerate stretched H4, where a PDS root slots BETWEEN two true levels and skips one entirely --
if that happens, the informative finding is that PDS roots track spectral DENSITY, not level INDEX,
which is a real distinction to document, not a bug to paper over. Do this only after (or alongside) the
centered-frame entry above, since at raw K=7 the roots are already conditioning garbage per that
entry's own scout probe.

Cost: cheap.
acceptance_criteria: pds_roots (or equivalent) returns the full sorted real-root array; validity (root_j >= E_j - 1e-9 Ha for all j) checked on H4 across K=3..8; usefulness checked against the 1.6 mHa-at-K=8 threshold; degeneracy/index-matching behavior on near-degenerate stretched H4 is explicitly tested and reported, including any index-skip failure mode.
notes: Done. pds_roots added to moment_expansion.py; pds_energy is now a thin wrapper (regression-checked against test_moment_pds_spec.py, still green). New spec specs/SPEC_pds_excited_roots.md + tests/test_pds_excited_roots_spec.py (5 gates: G1,G1b,G2,G3,G4), all passing, verified stable over 5+ fresh-process runs. G1 (bound) holds in its scoped regime (H4 eq K=3..8, stretched K=3..6). G2 (usefulness@K=8) KILLED as predicted: root_1 misses E_1 by 12-14 mHa, 8-9x the 1.6mHa bar. G4 (index-matching on near-degenerate stretched H4) KILLED as predicted: reachable level 2 is skipped by nearest-neighbor assignment at K=6. UNPLANNED finding (R3): at K=7 on the stretched geometry, even BLAS-thread-pinned, ~half of fresh-process runs VIOLATE the variational bound itself by -7.49 mHa (cond(M)~1.2e17) -- the bound is a theorem in exact arithmetic and float64 can break it once near-degenerate orbitals meet cond(M)>1e14. G1 scoped to exclude that cell; G1b pins cond(M)>1e14 as the falsifiable reason. Full writeup: sandbox-handoffs/chem-pc1.md. Tree left dirty per session git policy.
close_reason: Closed

title: PDS's accuracy floor (det M -> 0, capped at K<=4) may be a removable artifact of the uncentered moment frame
description:
specs/BACKLOG.md line ~251, "Method rungs" section (scout probe). Claim: SPEC_moment_pds's R1 calls
"det M -> 0 at large K" fundamental and caps gates at K<=4. It may not be fundamental: the moment
matrix inherits the dynamic range of raw electronic-frame moments (~||H||^n), and rebuilding the
identical moments in the repo's own centered frame (device_odmd.centered_frame already exists) is
reported to drop cond(M) by 12-18 orders of magnitude at IDENTICAL PDS values, which would unlock
K = 7-8.

Scout-probe evidence already in the backlog: N2 CAS(6,6), raw frame gives 0.044 mHa error at K=6 but
WORSENS to 0.049 mHa at K=7 -- non-monotone, violating the spec's own G3 monotone-tightening claim.
Centered frame stays monotone: 0.054 -> 0.006 -> 0.001 mHa over the same K range.

Check (killable): dies if centered != raw by >1e-6 Ha wherever raw cond(M) < 1e10 (i.e. they're not
actually the same functional once you account for conditioning), OR if centering fails to deliver
>=8 orders of magnitude cond(M) reduction at K=8.

Reuse (100% composition, zero new primitives needed): hamiltonian_moments, pds_energy,
device_odmd.centered_frame.

Caveat: this is numerical hygiene, not new physics -- it does NOT change PDS's asymptotic convergence
rate, only how far K can go before float64 quits. Also: mu (used to check monotonicity) comes from
dense diagonalization in the gate, which is a validation-scale-only technique -- the deliverable should
gate PDS's *sensitivity* to a badly estimated mu, not assume mu is free to compute in general.

Cost: cheap.
acceptance_criteria: Centered-frame PDS values agree with raw-frame values to <1e-6 Ha wherever raw cond(M)<1e10; cond(M) reduction at K=8 is measured and compared to the 8-order threshold; K=7-8 gates added if the reduction holds, with the N2 CAS(6,6) non-monotonicity either reproduced-and-fixed or shown absent in the centered frame.
close_reason: SURVIVES with amendment (PR #50, 2186f4c, worked from a cloud session). Centered vs raw PDS agree to 8.2e-12 Ha where raw cond<1e10; cond(M) cut at K=8: 13.0/11.3/17.4 orders (H4/LiH/N2), past the 8-order kill line. K=7-8 gates added (centered PDS variational+monotone to K=8). N2 raw non-monotonicity reproduced and shown BLAS-path dependent (up to 337 Ha below FCI). Amendment: K > n_reachable is fundamentally singular (H2, 2.3 orders) - gated as G2b. mu=<H> (free) suffices. Re-verified on linux/amd64 in claude-chem: 10 passed in 215s (gates abort on macOS LAPACK, chem-a0y).

title: The overlap certificate has no noise sibling -- predict and test whether its shot-noise coverage bifurcates instead of degrading smoothly
description:
specs/BACKLOG.md line ~236, "Certified-bounds arc" section. Claim: for a determinant guiding state
(the overlap certificate's u), lambda_u and r are classically exact -- zero shot noise -- so ALL noise
in the certificate enters through a single input, the gap floor beta, and gamma_min =
sqrt(1 - r^2/delta^2) has an UNBOUNDED derivative as r -> delta. Prediction: coverage (fraction of
seeded trials producing a valid, non-vacuous certificate) does not degrade smoothly with shot count --
it bifurcates: near-perfect coverage at wide margin (delta - r large), collapsing discontinuously at
thin margin. This would mean the guided-LH "coverage >= 1/poly" claim from related specs survives only
in the wide-margin regime, not generally.

Check (killable): >=6000 seeded trials, shots in {1e4, 1e5, 1e6}, z (inflation factor) in {0,1,2,3}, on
four systems spanning the margin from wide (H2 0.74 A, gamma=0.9936) to vacuous (square H4 1.2 A).
Dies if z<=2 restores coverage >=0.9 everywhere -- that would just repeat "inflation buys coverage,"
already shown elsewhere, and not be a new finding.

Reuse: certified_noise.shot_noise_coverage for the trial machinery; gap_selfcheck_noise._pad for the
post-hoc padding convention.

Caveat: the shot-free-residual argument is specific to determinant guiding states. A chained-Ritz
state (see the krylov_refine/SPEC_chained_overlap work) puts r back on the noise budget -- state that
scope boundary explicitly in whatever is written up, don't let it get discovered later as a surprise.

Cost: cheap.
acceptance_criteria: >=6000 seeded trials across the specified shots x z x system grid; coverage-vs-margin curve reported; the bifurcation-vs-smooth-degradation question is answered with the z<=2 kill criterion evaluated explicitly; the determinant-only scope caveat is stated in the writeup.
close_reason: Implemented specs/SPEC_hf_overlap_noise.md + hf_overlap_noise.py + tests/test_hf_overlap_noise_spec.py (10/10 green). Kill criterion (z<=2 restores coverage>=0.9 everywhere) evaluated explicitly and fails to kill the claim; found the sharper, unpredicted sign-reversal (inflation helps at wide margin, hurts at thin/moderate margin). Determinant-only scope caveat stated. See sandbox-handoffs/chem-mqu.md.

title: Quantify the certified sub-cluster anchor: can Krylov moments bound the HF weight eta on levels missed by an overshooting self-mode floor?
description:
specs/BACKLOG.md line ~223, "Certified-bounds arc" section (scout probe). Claim: the "certified
sub-cluster anchor" problem SPEC_subspace_floor_resolvability deferred as hard reduces to an exact
leakage correction -- if the self-mode floor beta overshoots the true E_d, the only damage is the HF
spectral weight eta on the missed levels, and gamma_corr = sqrt(1 - r^2/delta^2 - eta) is valid for
ANY beta (not just a tight one). So the open question becomes: can Krylov data (S_0k, the Fourier
moments of the HF spectral measure -- already computed by the solver, no extra work) bound eta from
above?

Scout-probe evidence already in the backlog: measured eta = 2.4e-2 / 3.8e-2 / 7.4e-2 on the spec's
three escape witnesses, spanning 54-142 levels each -- i.e. NOT the "one tiny missed level" story the
original spec told, but beta overshooting by 0.22-0.33 Ha and sweeping a whole band.

Check (killable): G-a, validity of gamma_corr on the spec's own escape witnesses (should hold by
construction -- confirm it does). G-b, the actual killer: bound eta from the Krylov moments S_0k and
compare to the measured eta above. Dies if the moment bound exceeds ~0.05 at M<=24.

Caveat (the author's own prediction, worth taking seriously): G-b is expected to be killed. That is
the point, not a failure mode to avoid -- a kill converts "open problem, deferred" into a falsifiable,
quantified design target: "needs Krylov resolution 1/(M*Delta_t) below the floor overshoot, measured
at 0.22-0.33 Ha." Write that up as the result if it happens.

Cost: medium.
acceptance_criteria: gamma_corr validity confirmed on the three escape witnesses (G-a); a Krylov-moment bound on eta is derived and compared against the measured eta = 2.4e-2/3.8e-2/7.4e-2 (G-b); the pass/fail against the 0.05-at-M<=24 threshold is recorded either way, including a full kill (which converts the finding into a quantified resolution requirement, not a dead end).

Pre-existing: identical with or without the chem-0tb lint fix. The file was committed mid-bead in the 5c5c6db snapshot, so these may be the worker's in-progress state rather than a regression -- confirm before relying on G-b.

title: build_molecular_hamiltonian hardcodes PySCFDriver with no conv_tol -- every recorded result uses the SCF default that sits on a known artifact
description:

title: Rewire ~13 reachability-threshold sites onto the symmetry-aware filter
description:
specs/BACKLOG.md line ~69 (top-level, under "## Open"). Claim: SPEC_symmetry_reachability (done
2026-08) built a symmetry/sector-aware reachability decision in reachability.py, but it was

title: Two robot D2/D3 spec tests import certkit unconditionally, breaking full-suite collection
description:
Reproduced 2026-09-28: after the documented setup (`uv sync --extra dmrg --extra test`, no
`--extra certkit`), `uv run pytest --collect-only -q tests/` reports 762 tests collected and 2
collection ERRORS:
  tests/test_robot_workspace_d2_spec.py:4  ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'certkit'
  tests/test_robot_failclosed_d3_spec.py:3 ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'certkit'

title: Documented setup command leaves ruff uninstalled; `make lint`/ruff unusable
description:
Reproduced 2026-09-28: `uv sync --extra dmrg --extra test` (the exact command CLAUDE.md documents
as setup) completes cleanly, but the resulting environment has no `ruff` binary. `uv run ruff check .`
then fails with `error: Failed to spawn: 'ruff' / cause: No such file or directory (os error 2)`.

Root cause: pyproject.toml's `[project.optional-dependencies]` puts `ruff>=0.5` under the `dev` group,
not `test` or `dmrg`. `make lint` runs `ruff check .` directly and would hit the same failure in any
environment built via the documented setup path.

Confirmed the fix path works: `uv sync --extra dev` (or adding `--extra dev` to the documented command)
installs ruff, and `uv run ruff check .` then reports `All checks passed!` with zero violations — so
this is a packaging/doc gap, not a real lint failure.

title: Committed NbN SCF reference (data/nbn_scf.chk, S=3 sector) sits at a threading-nondeterministic, marginally-unstable UHF solution
description: chem-owr diagnosed why nbn_low_spin.py scan doesn't reproduce the committed chk energy at d=3.7255 A: it is NOT a geometry/basis/ECP/MIC bug in the scan reconstruction (all verified identical to <2e-5 A and identical basis/ECP assignment). The root cause is that the committed high-spin (10,4)/S=3 UHF solution sits essentially exactly at a pyscf internal-stability boundary (a near-zero Hessian eigenvalue in benchmark_nbn._tight_scf's stability-following loop). Whether pyscf's Davidson-based stability() call reports 'stable' (keeping the higher-energy committed solution) or 'unstable' (following it down 0.548 mHa in SCF / 4.84 mHa in downstream CAS(14,14) FCI(10,4)) depends on default multi-threaded BLAS floating-point non-associativity: with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, two independent fresh SCF runs on the real geometry (specs/nbn_mp-2634.cif) deterministically and reproducibly (bit-identical, e_tot=-110.02813374576796 both times) find the instability and land on the LOWER, more-stable solution; with default multi-threading, 3 of 4 trials found the same lower solution but 1 of 4 reproduced the committed higher (metastable) energy (-110.02758538272639, matching specs/nbn_scf_reference.chk's -110.0275853827266 to 9 decimals). This means the currently-vendored NbN SCF reference (specs/nbn_scf_reference.chk / data/nbn_scf.chk), and every number built on it across nbn_dmrg_reference.py, SPEC_nbn_dmrg_reference.md (G1-G3b), and SPEC_nbn_low_spin.md (Tables 1-2, the S1-S3 gap, the G4/G5 gates), is anchored to a UHF solution that the SAME current code, run deterministically (single-threaded), reproducibly finds is NOT the lowest/most-stable one available in the (10,4) sector. Needs: (1) decide whether to re-vendor a chk from the deterministic single-threaded lower-energy solution, or keep the current one with an explicit caveat that it is metastable; (2) if re-vendored, every downstream gate/table anchored to the old chk's energy needs re-deriving, which is substantial (touches chem-bbi's G3/G3b, chem-g1i's Tables 1-3/G4/G5 -- both already-closed beads). title: tests/test_lambda_ladder_honest_caveat_spec.py::test_G3 and test_shift_both_sides_spec.py::test_G5[H2] flaky: RHF/CASCI orbital gauge nondeterminism for degenerate systems
description:
Discovered while verifying chem-3f8's fix (unrelated to it -- reproduces identically on the original unmodified lambda_ladder.py/shift_both_sides.py via git stash, confirmed the fix did not cause it). Two spec gates are flaky across repeated 'uv run pytest' invocations in fresh processes, same inputs, same code:

1. tests/test_lambda_ladder_honest_caveat_spec.py::test_G3_df_rank_truncation_accuracy_is_not_monotonic (N2 CAS(4,3), sto-3g) -- asserts the DF rank-truncation FCI-error sweep is NOT monotonically decreasing (the spec's documented finding). Failed 2/5 runs; the per-rank error sequence itself differs numerically between process runs (e.g. one run: [77.03, 74.98, 6.59, 49.41, 50.15, 0.0] mHa: clearly non-monotonic and passes; another: [127.13, 99.63, 46.39, 42.26, 11.65, 5.7e-11]: monotonically decreasing and fails) even though double_factorize()'s g eigenvalues are close but not exactly degenerate (0.0846, 0.0763, 0.0691, 0.0561, 0.0451 -- see df_factorization.double_factorize output for this system).

2. tests/test_shift_both_sides_spec.py::test_G5_identity_term_inflates_the_gain[H2] -- 'assert inflated > honest' flips sign between runs (e.g. one run: inflated=2.563, honest=3.071 -- fails; the intent is inflated>honest).

Root cause not yet isolated but the leading suspect is RHF converging to an arbitrary rotation within a near-degenerate orbital subspace (N2's pi pair is exactly degenerate by symmetry; H2's minimal-basis case may have a similar near-tie) that varies run-to-run, likely from BLAS/LAPACK thread-count nondeterminism in eigh/SCF diagonalization -- NOT from double_factorize's own eigh call in isolation (repeated eigh calls on the SAME eri within one process are deterministic; the eri itself differs across fresh-process runs). Needs isolating whether it's mf.kernel()'s SCF orbitals, cas.kernel()'s CASCI step, or double_factorize's eigh that is the nondeterministic step, then either pinning BLAS threads (OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 / OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1) for reproducibility, or fixing the gauge (e.g. canonicalize degenerate-subspace orbitals) before these specs' assertions, or loosening/re-deriving the acceptance thresholds if the finding is gauge-dependent rather than a fixed fact about these systems.
acceptance_criteria: Both tests pass deterministically across >=10 repeated fresh-process pytest runs (or the spec is revised to state the gauge-dependence honestly, per specs/README.md's 'if a gate proves unsatisfiable, revise the spec and record why').
notes: LOCAL macOS RE-VERIFICATION 2026-09-27: acceptance NOT met. test_G5[H2] fails 7/7 fresh runs deterministically (inflated=4.701 vs honest=3.071; sandbox Linux got inflated=2.56). ROOT CAUSE (neither the BLAS-gauge story nor the 'deterministic counter-example' story): for even norb (H2 norb=2, N2(6,6) norb=6) lambda_DF is EXACTLY flat in b2 around the SCDF optimum (nuclear norm of h1+b2*I constant while b2 sits between the middle eigenvalues), so df_factorization.symmetry_shift's Nelder-Mead b2 is arbitrary/platform-dependent. The identity-inclusive lambda_meas varies linearly along that flat line (H2: 1.11-1.44 for b2 +/-0.1, lambda_DF fixed at 0.970698); N2's honest lambda_meas also moves at b2-0.1. H2O(4,3) (odd norb) has a unique optimum. So H2/N2 inclusive gains (and the N2 'inflated>12' headline) are optimizer-endpoint artifacts. The original committed '53.9%/4.70x' H2 row was NOT wrong -- it is exactly what macOS computes; the chem-1yr revision to 2.56x is equally arbitrary. Needs: canonical b2 tie-break on the flat interval, or restate G5 as b2-gauge-dependent for even norb.
close_reason: Local macOS re-verification found the real G5[H2] cause: lambda_DF is exactly flat in b2 for even norb, so Nelder-Mead's b2 was arbitrary per platform and moved only the identity-inclusive gain (macOS 4.70x, Linux 2.56x). The H2 'exception' is retracted. symmetry_shift now sets b2 analytically at the flat interval's midpoint (lambda_DF unchanged, H2O identical). G5 is back to 'every molecule' (5.33/4.24/14.32x inclusive vs 3.07/2.73/5.67x honest). Both gate files pass 10/10 fresh-process runs; scdf_lambda/precision_cost gates green. SPEC_shift_both_sides.md R3-R4.

title: Certified two-sided H-chain bracket: VSDP-rigorous PQG+T2 lower bound + DMRG upper, n=12-16
description: Discovery shortlist #2 (portfolio notes/discovery-shortlist.md), verdict PARTIAL. Chaykin, Jansson, Keil et al. title: Implement SPEC_interval_dominance_screening: prune candidate libraries by certified bracket dominance
description:
Implement specs/SPEC_interval_dominance_screening.md (Proposed v1.0): use certified energy brackets at cheap Krylov dimension to prove a candidate cannot be the global minimum (L_j > U_best) and prune it before paying for full convergence.

Deliverables: screening_loop.py, tests/test_screening_loop_spec.py (G1-G4), data/screening_loop_performance.csv, spec revised to v2.0, BACKLOG entry.

REVIEW FLAGS (resolve or falsify, do not tune around):
1. LIKELY KILL - bracket looseness at cheap M. Pruning needs L_j(M) > U_best. SPEC_excited_state_certification just measured certified bracket widths of 88.3 mHa (LiH) and 981 mHa (H4) at low M, and temple_bounds lower bounds are looser still at M=2. If the M=2 bracket is hundreds of mHa wide, NOTHING prunes and the 75-80 percent saving is unreachable. Measure the actual bracket width vs the actual candidate spread FIRST, before building the loop - that single number decides whether this spec lives.
2. LIBRARY DEPENDENCE. The specced library is a geometry sweep of ONE molecule, whose candidates sit within mHa of each other near the minimum - the worst case for interval dominance. Savings are a property of the library's energy spread relative to bracket width, not of the method. Any percentage must be quoted with the library that produced it, and the spread/width ratio is the real gated quantity.
3. G3 'strictly non-increasing staircase' is VACUOUS - an active pool can only shrink by construction. Replace with a gate on how EARLY pruning happens (pool size at each M), which is what the economic claim rests on.
4. No QPU is involved. 'Saving QPU runtime' is simulated circuit/shot accounting; the cost model must be stated and its assumptions gated.
5. G1 zero-false-negatives is the soundness gate and matters most - a prune that drops the true winner invalidates everything. Test it against brute force on a library where brackets nearly overlap.
acceptance_criteria: make gates-screening_loop green; G1 soundness (no false prune of the true winner) proven against brute force; the achievable saving reported with the library spread/bracket-width ratio that produced it, or the spec honestly killed if cheap-M brackets cannot dominate; spec at v2.0 with v1.0 preserved; ruff clean; nothing committed without approval

title: Implement SPEC_trotter_floor_restorer: pre-diagonalization Richardson on Trotter signals

Implement specs/SPEC_trotter_floor_restorer.md (Proposed v1.0): extrapolate the complex Trotter survival-amplitude signal BEFORE diagonalization, so the variational-floor leak is plugged while Ritz vectors and variances survive for Lehmann certification (excited_bounds.py).

1. TIME-ALIGNMENT BUG in spec 3.2. s_k(dt) sits at physical time k*dt, s_k(2dt) at 2k*dt. Richardson across the same index k compares DIFFERENT times, so the O(dt^2) term does not cancel. Correct pairing is likely s_2k(dt) vs s_k(2dt). Check before implementing; if the spec formula is wrong, that is the first finding.
2. G2 demands the restored energy sit ABOVE E_FCI. Richardson error is two-sided and ODMD/Krylov on an extrapolated signal is NOT variational (SPEC_odmd G2 already gates that). 'E >= E_FCI' is probably not a guarantee, only an observation at particular dt. Gate what is true.
3. G4 says 2x narrower than 'any attempt' to bound scalar_extrap - unfalsifiable as written. Needs one concrete named scalar-extrap bound to compare against.
4. G3 '100% sound across all step-sizes' - check whether soundness survives large dt where the Trotter sector itself shifts.

title: Nb3Cl8 parameter-free cluster optical gap hits the measured absorption edge -- test the family trend and the thermal-collapse prediction that would falsify it
